Hi Ben / Samantha,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — really helpful to understand BrightCart's intended usage patterns and procurement cadence. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a Marketplace private offer path: 

Recap
- Primary use: semantic search + summarization for customer support and product pages.
- Expected token volumes (initial): 50M - 200M tokens/month depending on rollout waves; potential to grow beyond that in 2027.
- Key requirements: SOC 2 evidence, option for private deployment later (VPC), and predictable unit economics for budgeting.

Pricing questions we discussed
- Target unit economics: BrightCart mentioned aiming for ~ $30–$60 / 1M tokens depending on volume tiers.
- You asked about how Redwood's unit price maps to an AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace private offer — who absorbs marketplace fees, and what the customer-facing unit price should look like.

What I need from you to move forward
1) Confirmation of projected month 1 and month 6 token volumes (ballpark numbers are fine).
2) Procurement timeline and who will negotiate the private offer on the BrightCart side (legal/procurement contact).
3) Are you open to AWS Marketplace private offer for initial purchase, or do you prefer Azure Marketplace? (Samantha, any notes on cross-marketplace mechanics are welcome.)

How we usually map unit price to marketplace listings
- Redwood provides a net unit price we need to receive (example: $40 / 1M tokens).
- Marketplace billing layer typically requires listing a customer price that accounts for marketplace fees and any passthroughs.
- We can propose a mapping table and draft private offer lineup for the tiers you need — I’ll attach a starter spreadsheet.

Next steps
- Ben: can you share the procurement contact and confirm volumes?
- Samantha: any quick guidance on private offer steps and requirements from the AWS side (AM account ID, seller listing requirements)?
- Aditya: I’ll ask you to finalize the draft pricing table once Ben provides volumes.

I attached a draft pricing worksheet with an example mapping that shows how a Redwood net price converts to a marketplace unit price. Happy to hop on a 30m sync next week to finalize.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Marissa / Ben — thanks for the ping. Happy to help coordinate the AWS Marketplace private offer path. A few items to note from the AWS side: 

Marketplace private offer basics
- Private offers allow a seller (Redwood) and buyer (BrightCart) to negotiate customized pricing and terms. The customer accepts the private offer from their AWS console.
- We will need the customer AWS account ID and the seller listing to be live with a metered product or SaaS listing configured.

Fees and pricing mapping
- Marketplace collects a fee associated with the transaction; private offers can include the marketplace fee in the listed price or be structured so the seller absorbs it (that’s negotiable).
- To model pricing accurately, we generally ask sellers to provide a net target (what Redwood needs to net) and we’ll work with Marketplace finance to estimate the listed price that achieves that after fees and any tax considerations.

What I need from you to move forward
1) Proposed net unit price tiers (net to Redwood) for the volumes Marissa/BrightCart shared.
2) Seller account ID (Redwood Marketplace account) and a link to the product listing (or let me know if you want AWS to enable a draft listing).
3) Customer AWS account ID (BrightCart) when you’re ready to create a private offer.

If you can share the pricing spreadsheet Marissa mentioned, I can run a quick mapping with our finance contact and confirm approximate listed prices and expected payout timing. Happy to join a sync with procurement/legal if helpful.

— Samantha
Samantha Liu | Partner Sales, AWS Marketplace
samantha.liu@amazon.com

Subject: Re: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer & unit price mapping

Thanks Ben / Samantha — sending the draft mapping and a few worked examples inline below to make the mechanics concrete.

Example unit price mapping (illustrative)
- Redwood net price: $40.00 / 1M tokens (net to Redwood)
- Marketplace fee estimate (example): 5%
- Listed marketplace price = Redwood_net / (1 - marketplace_fee) ≈ $40 / 0.95 ≈ $42.11 → rounded to $42.50 / 1M tokens
- If Redwood prefers to list a round number to customers, we can propose $45 / 1M tokens as the public/private-offer price; after the fee the net to Redwood would be ~$42.75 (example).

Tiered proposal (sample)
- 0–50M tokens/mo: Redwood net $55 / 1M → listed ~$57.90 → propose $59.99
- 50–200M tokens/mo: Redwood net $42 / 1M → listed ~$44.21 → propose $44.99
- 200M+ tokens/mo: Redwood net $35 / 1M → listed ~$36.84 → propose $36.99

Notes
- These are examples to show how fees and rounding affect the customer-facing unit price. We can adjust the fee assumption depending on the actual Marketplace program and whether Redwood chooses to absorb all/part of the fee.
- I attached the pricing worksheet with a formula tab so you can plug in your preferred net price and marketplace fee and get the corresponding listed price automatically.

Attachments: brightcart_pricing_draft.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_marketplace_mapping.csv (csv)

Proposed next steps
1) Ben: please introduce Alice (procurement) and share BrightCart AWS account ID if you want to proceed on AWS.
2) Samantha: once we confirm Redwood seller account ID and the listing, can you run a quick estimate with Marketplace finance?
3) Aditya: can you finalize the sheet and include a column for estimated annual spend (for AWS finance)?

I’m available for a 30m call Tues 7/14 or Wed 7/15 to finalize the tiers and sign-off on a private offer.

Thanks,
Marissa
